newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to implement reforms for economy - MOF quoted.
newsitem.headline: Japan to implement reforms for economy - MOF quoted.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying on Tuesday that Japan will steadily implement reforms, the supplementary budget for this fiscal year and the full state budget for next fiscal year for the sake of the economy, including the stock market.
Mitsuzuka was quoted by Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso as telling cabinet ministers with economic portfolios that the economy is generally on a steady recovery track.
Mitsuzuka also said he was watching the stock market, which is worried about the prospects for the economy, with great interest, Aso said.
The finance minister told the ministers that he will take worries in the market seriously and do his utmost to help manage the economy in cooperation with the government and political parties.

Japan will steadily and quickly implement the reforms in areas outlined by the government. It will work towards passing the supplementary budget for 1996/97 and the full budget for 1997/98 without delay so that there will be no gaps in government spending, Mitsuzuka said.

He also said it was up to the current government to steadily implement the reforms and asked for public understanding. The government is planning to set up a meeting of experts for fiscal reform and the finance minister hopes to actively take part in it. He also hopes the decisions made in the meeting will be reflected in the 1997/98 state budget.

Mitsuzuka said he would take special care in overseeing Japan's financial system and industries and promote reforms, such as by submitting a revision for the foreign exchange law in this session of parliament.
He said he would make his best efforts to draw out the vitality of the Japanese economy from both the fiscal and monetary side.

Aso quoted Taku Yamazaki, chairman of the policy-making committee of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party, as telling ministers that he had been asked by a senior LDP official to consider measures to deal with stock price falls.

Yamazaki said although he realised it was important to implement reforms and pass the budget, he questioned whether the government thought it was necessary to come up with measures to cope with stock falls toward book closings in March.
The MOF minister was quoted as saying that the government for now will carry out structural reforms.

Kabun Muto, the head of the government's Management and Coordination Agency, was quoted as saying that the government and parties needed to consider ways to make the Japan stock market more attractive.
Aso declined to give his view of recent stock falls, but did say that economic indicators were not moving in a bad direction.
He also said that he did not know if government ministers were meeting to discuss the economy on Tuesday but LDP officials were planning to meet to possibly discuss stocks.
